name: Pabna
tagline: Where the Padma is spanned by century-old steel — the twin bridges of Paksey, the double-roofed Jor Bangla, gawa ghee, handloom saris, and the home town of a screen legend.

guide.bestTime: October to March — dry, cool weather, the best light on the Padma and comfortable days for the riverside and the out-of-town mosques and temples.
guide.gettingThere: By road from Dhaka (~160 km, ~4–5 hr) via the Bangabandhu Bridge, or from Rajshahi (~75 km). By rail the district is served through Ishwardi Junction — one of the largest junctions in the country — with a connecting service to Pabna town. There is also a Padma ferry/launch crossing at Kazirhat on the Aricha route.
guide.difficulty: Easy — the town sights are walkable or a short rickshaw ride, and Paksey, Chatmohar and Ishwardi are comfortable day trips by bus or CNG.

mustVisit.name: Hardinge Bridge & Lalon Shah Bridge (Paksey)
mustVisit.description: Two great bridges side by side over the Padma at Paksey — the steel railway truss of Hardinge Bridge and, running parallel, the road deck of the Lalon Shah Bridge — the district's defining view of the river.
mustVisit.history: Hardinge Bridge, about 1.8 km long, was engineered in England by Sir Alexander Meadows Rendel and built between 1910 and 1912; trains began running in 1915 and it was formally opened by the Viceroy, Lord Hardinge, on 4 March 1915. The road bridge alongside it, named after the mystic poet Lalon Shah, was inaugurated in 2004.

practical.hours: Riverside viewing any time; best by daylight
practical.entryFee: Free to view from the banks

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: At Paksey in Ishwardi upazila, on the Padma toward Bheramara/Kushtia
howToReach.transport: Bus or CNG to Ishwardi/Paksey from Pabna town

mustVisit.bestTime: Late afternoon for the light on the river and the steelwork
tips: The railway bridge is an active line — view it from the bank, not the track
Combine with the Paksey riverside and a look at the Padma from the road bridge

mustVisit.name: Jor Bangla Temple
mustVisit.description: A brick temple just outside Pabna town, named for its distinctive 'jor bangla' double-pitched roof that echoes the thatched huts of rural Bengal — once richly clad in terracotta.
mustVisit.history: Local tradition holds it was built in the mid-18th century by Brajmohan Krori, a tahsildar of the Nawab of Murshidabad, though no inscription survives to confirm the date. Its terracotta ornament was damaged in the great earthquake of 1897.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 2 km north-east of Pabna town centre

mustVisit.bestTime: Morning, for soft light on the brickwork
tips: Look closely at the surviving terracotta detailing on the walls
Dress modestly and be respectful at the shrine

mustVisit.name: Tarash Bhaban
mustVisit.description: A 19th-century zamindar mansion on Hamid Road in the heart of Pabna town — a handsome relic of the district's landed-gentry past, set among the everyday bustle of the modern town.
mustVisit.history: The building was raised in the 1800s by Banamali Roy Bahadur, one of the leading zamindars of Pabna. (Despite the name, the mansion stands in Pabna town — not in the Tarash upazila of neighbouring Sirajganj.)

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: On Hamid Road, central Pabna town

tips: Parts are in government/institutional use — view the façade respectfully
Pair it with a short heritage walk around the old town

mustVisit.name: Suchitra Sen's Memorial Home
mustVisit.description: The ancestral family home of the legendary actress Suchitra Sen, on Hem Sagar Lane in Pabna town — where she spent her childhood — now kept as a modest memorial to one of Bengali cinema's greatest stars.
mustVisit.history: The house at Gopalpur, Hem Sagar Lane, was recovered by the district administration after a long legal battle in 2014 and turned into a memorial holding a statue and a collection relating to her films. (Sources differ on her exact birthplace, but the family home and her upbringing were here in Pabna.)

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Hem Sagar Lane, central Pabna town

tips: It is a small, low-key memorial — come for the connection, not a grand museum
Ask locally for current opening arrangements before visiting

mustVisit.name: Chatmohar Shahi Mosque
mustVisit.description: A three-domed Mughal mosque at Chatmohar — one of the oldest surviving Mughal monuments in this part of Bengal, built of thin 'jafari' bricks.
mustVisit.history: An inscription dates the mosque to 1582 (989 AH), placing it among the earliest Mughal-era buildings in the region. It measures roughly 45 by 22.5 feet beneath its three domes.

practical.hours: Daylight hours; an active mosque — avoid prayer times for sightseeing

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: In Chatmohar upazila, north-east of Pabna town
howToReach.transport: Bus or CNG to Chatmohar from Pabna town

tips: Dress modestly and remove shoes to enter
Be quiet and unobtrusive — it remains in daily use for worship

mustVisit.name: The Padma at Paksey & Kazirhat
mustVisit.description: The wide, slow Padma defines Pabna's western and southern edge — best felt from the Paksey riverside beneath the bridges, or from the Kazirhat ferry ghat where launches and ferries cross the great river.
mustVisit.history: Kazirhat became Pabna's main Padma crossing on the Aricha route after the old Nagarbari terminal was shifted following the opening of the Bangabandhu Bridge; the river has always been the district's lifeline for trade and travel.

practical.hours: Daylight for the river views; ferries run on their own schedule

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Paksey ~28 km west (Ishwardi); Kazirhat ghat to the south of the district
howToReach.transport: Bus/CNG to Paksey or Kazirhat from Pabna town

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool, dry months at golden hour
tips: Sunset over the Padma from Paksey is the photograph to wait for
Mind the currents — the Padma is powerful; stay on the banks and jetties

specialties.name: Pabnar Gawa Ghee
specialties.description: Pabna's most famous product — clarified butter slow-simmered the old way over wood fires until it turns deep gold and intensely fragrant. Pabna town's ghee shops have made it a name known across the country.

specialties.name: Pabna Handloom Sari
specialties.description: Cotton saris woven on handlooms in a tradition that reaches back to the Mughal period — a livelihood for a vast number of weaving families across the district and part of Bangladesh's recognised handloom heritage.
specialties.venue: Handloom weaving villages and Pabna town markets

specialties.name: Ishwardi Mango
specialties.description: Ishwardi, in the mango belt of greater Rajshahi, ripens sweet summer mangoes that fill the markets through the season.

bucketlist.title: See the Hardinge Bridge over the Padma
bucketlist.detail: A 1.8 km steel railway bridge opened in 1915, engineered in England — the district's signature landmark at Paksey.

bucketlist.title: Watch the sun set over the Padma at Paksey
bucketlist.detail: The wide river glows gold beneath the twin bridges — the photograph worth waiting for.

bucketlist.title: Find the double-roofed Jor Bangla Temple
bucketlist.detail: A mid-18th-century brick temple just outside town, named for its 'jor bangla' twin-pitched roof and once clad in terracotta.

bucketlist.title: Walk past Tarash Bhaban
bucketlist.detail: A 19th-century zamindar mansion on Hamid Road, a relic of Pabna's landed past in the heart of the town.

bucketlist.title: Visit Suchitra Sen's memorial home
bucketlist.detail: The childhood family home of the legendary actress, kept as a modest memorial on Hem Sagar Lane.

bucketlist.title: See the 1582 Chatmohar Shahi Mosque
bucketlist.detail: A three-domed Mughal mosque of thin jafari bricks — among the oldest surviving Mughal monuments in the region.

bucketlist.title: Taste real Pabnar gawa ghee
bucketlist.detail: Deep-gold clarified butter slow-cooked over wood fires — Pabna's most famous flavour, bought straight from the town's ghee shops.

bucketlist.title: Buy a Pabna handloom sari
bucketlist.detail: Cotton woven on handlooms in a tradition reaching back to Mughal times — bought near the weaving villages.

bucketlist.title: Eat Ishwardi mango in season
bucketlist.detail: Sweet summer mangoes from the orchards of Ishwardi, in the greater Rajshahi mango belt.

bucketlist.title: Cross the Padma from Kazirhat
bucketlist.detail: Take the ferry or launch across the great river from Pabna's main Padma ghat at Kazirhat.

bucketlist.title: Pass through Ishwardi Junction
bucketlist.detail: One of the largest railway junctions in the country and Pabna's gateway to the national rail network.

bucketlist.title: Wander old Pabna town
bucketlist.detail: Stitch together Tarash Bhaban, the Suchitra Sen home and the riverside lanes on an unhurried heritage walk.

foods.name: Gawa Ghee
foods.description: Pabna's celebrated clarified butter, slow-simmered over wood fires to a deep gold — fragrant enough to be eaten simply over hot rice.

foods.name: Ishwardi Mango
foods.description: Sweet seasonal mangoes from the orchards of Ishwardi in the greater Rajshahi mango belt.

foods.name: Padma River Fish
foods.description: Freshwater fish from the Padma — including hilsa in season — fried fresh or in light curries at riverside eateries.

foods.name: Khejur Gur
foods.description: Date-palm jaggery from the winter harvest, used in the season's sweets and eaten with pithas across the region.

famousPeople.name: Bande Ali Mia
famousPeople.knownFor: Beloved poet, lyricist, novelist and children's writer, born at Radhanagar in Pabna; author of some eighty books and recipient of the Bangla Academy Award (1962) and Ekushey Padak (1988).

famousPeople.name: Suchitra Sen
famousPeople.knownFor: One of the greatest stars of Bengali (and Hindi) cinema — Devdas, Saat Pake Bandha, Aandhi — and the first Indian actress to win an international acting prize, at the 1963 Moscow Film Festival. Her ancestral family home, where she grew up, is in Pabna town.

didYouKnow: The Pabna Mental Hospital at Hemayetpur, founded in 1957, is the only government-run mental hospital in all of Bangladesh.
Hardinge Bridge, the ~1.8 km steel railway bridge over the Padma at Paksey, was engineered in England, completed in 1912 and formally opened by Viceroy Lord Hardinge in 1915.
Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant is being built at Rooppur in Pabna's Ishwardi upazila — the site was first chosen back in 1963.
The legendary actress Suchitra Sen grew up in Pabna town, and her ancestral home there is now kept as a memorial.
Pabna's handloom saris trace back to the Mughal era, and the Chatmohar Shahi Mosque of 1582 is among the oldest surviving Mughal monuments in the region.
